notes.repograph_store: branch bench/three-graphs-2026-09-04 @ 7479a02 (`repograph --version` still prints 0.4.0). Built with `repograph --repo . build`, no `enrich`, no `--rerank`: 8316 nodes / 32601 edges, 32M on disk (.repograph/), 139s wall (1s lexical pass over 908 changed files, 135s dense-embedding 7408 rows).
notes.graphify_graph: rebuilt 2026-09-04 via `graphify update . --force` in the scratch worktree: 26634 nodes / 50947 edges, 1403 communities, 123M on disk, 23s wall, 0 tokens (AST re-extraction off the warm semantic cache; two files had syntax errors and contributed no symbols: packages/domain/src/registry/index.ts, packages/domain/src/schedule/index.ts).
notes.gitnexus_index: analyzed 2026-09-04 via `gitnexus analyze -f --embeddings --skip-agents-md .`: 26801 nodes / 43745 edges, 652 clusters, 300 flows, 7954 local embeddings, 598M on disk, 215s wall. `--skip-agents-md` held: git status showed no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md diff. `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` still appeared unasked (trap 1) and was removed after the run.
notes.gitnexus_repo_resolution_bug: HARNESS DEFECT, reported not fixed: run.py's default --gitnexus-repo is Path(args.repo).resolve().name, i.e. the corpus directory's basename. gitnexus registers a repo by a name it derives itself (here, 'beauty-crm', from both the real clone and the worktree), not by directory name, so a scratch worktree named anything else -- which the runbook itself mandates, to keep the working clone untouched -- matches no registered name. `gitnexus impact`/`trace`/`detect-changes` then print a JSON {"error": "...not found..."} on exit 1 and `gitnexus query` crashes with an uncaught RegistryAmbiguousTargetError-adjacent stack trace; run.py captures both as the tool's 'answer' regardless of exit code. Worse: the error JSON echoes the query back (e.g. `"to": {"name": "AvailabilityService"}`), so trace's substring check scored 2 false-positive hits before this was caught. First attempt at this run (discarded) scored gitnexus 0/82 retrieval, 0.0 impact recall, and a corrupted 2/8 trace via this bug. Worked around, without touching bench/compare/, by passing `--gitnexus-repo /private/tmp/bench-corpus-3g` (the worktree's absolute path), which both resolves correctly and disambiguates the two registry entries named 'beauty-crm' (the real beauty-crm clone, stale at 91970ba4, and this worktree, at 502e8a6d). The numbers in this file are from the corrected invocation.
notes.graphify_impact_refusals: `affected` refused an ambiguous name for 4 of 16 targets -- DatabaseService (hub), TenantContextInterceptor (narrow), ActorResolver (wide), OutboxPublisher (wide) -- the identical four names refused on 2026-09-03. Scored as 0 recall on those targets, not skipped, per the suite's own rule.
notes.gitnexus_changes_cap: `detect-changes` prints 15 changed symbols then `... and N more` regardless of `-l 500` (confirmed by hand: `-l 5` prints 5, `-l 500` still prints 15 -- the flag does not raise the CLI's display cap, only what it reports on top of it). The scored table uses the CLI number, per protocol. Hand-read via the `detect_changes` MCP tool for base `cbc931ba~1` (as the 2026-09-03 run did for the same base): the full payload lists 127 changed symbols and names 20 of the 21 the truth file wants (all but `HEAVY`), against 0/21 from the CLI's first-15 window -- the 21 real code symbols sit behind ~78 Markdown section titles the diff also touched. Not hand-checked for the other 7 bases; the gap is likely similar in shape (large diffs bury code symbols behind doc sections) but was not measured.
notes.truth: impact truth blanks comments and string literals before counting a reference (this run's reason for existing: this changed the old 10-target denominator from 114 to 111, per the task brief -- not independently re-derived here, since the old case file is a different, smaller suite). changes truth does not blank comments -- open caveat, see three-graphs.md. truth.py's ripgrep call runs with stdin detached (`stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL`); confirmed present and necessary -- this session is itself a non-interactive process.
notes.repograph_paraphrase_floor: the zero-token store (no `enrich`) scores paraphrase 9/30, confirmed twice: once via `bench/compare/run.py`'s plain `ask`, once via `repograph bench` run directly against the same store, which exits 1 with 'bench floors not met' against the shipped 14/30 floor. This is expected, not a regression: README documents that 'a store that enrich has never touched reads 40/40, 9/30, 12/12' -- the 14/30 floor presumes enrich-generated questions, which this run deliberately did not build, to keep the three tools' build cost comparable at zero tokens each.
